label: Town of Rockingham
header:
# Town of Rockingham municipal roster backfill -- Vermont
# municipal fan-out batch 19; issue #163 (VT master tracking).

sources.note: 17 V.S.A. section 2646: towns elect a moderator for a one-year term
The Commons, report of the March 3, 2026 Rockingham Australian ballot (newspaper source, disclosed; the town posts no 2026 results document): Paul Obuchowski was re-elected Moderator, uncontested

Town of Rockingham, 2025 Annual Report (July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025), 'TOWN OF ROCKINGHAM ELECTED OFFICIALS 2024-2025' table and the printed 2026 warning, read in the town's document library: Paul Obuchowski, Moderator (March 2025 - March 2026). He is also the Village of Bellows Falls Village President; the membership reuses that person record
17 V.S.A. section 2646: towns elect a town clerk

Town of Rockingham, 2025 Annual Report (July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025), 'TOWN OF ROCKINGHAM ELECTED OFFICIALS 2024-2025' table and the printed 2026 warning, read in the town's document library: Kathleen Kelly, Town Clerk (March 2025 - March 2028); the seat did not stand in 2026
Town of Rockingham, Town Clerk page (rockinghamvt.org): Kathleen Kelly is the Town Clerk. She is also the Village of Bellows Falls Village Clerk; the membership reuses that person record
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, and County Officials' (January 2026): lists Kathleen Kelly as Rockingham's Town Clerk
17 V.S.A. section 2646: towns elect a town treasurer

Town of Rockingham, 2025 Annual Report (July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025), 'TOWN OF ROCKINGHAM ELECTED OFFICIALS 2024-2025' table and the printed 2026 warning, read in the town's document library: Kathleen Kelly, Town Treasurer (March 2025 - March 2028); the seat did not stand in 2026
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, and County Officials' (January 2026): lists Kathleen Kelly as Rockingham's Town Treasurer

Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Selectboard Members' directory (updated June 5, 2026): lists three of Rockingham's five selectboard members: Dalila Hall, Amy Howlett, and Bonnie North (the directory's Rockingham entry is truncated)
Town of Rockingham, Selectboard page (rockinghamvt.org): the current board is Rick Cowan, John Dunbar, Amy Howlett, Bonnie North, and Dalila Hall

The Commons, report of the March 3, 2026 Rockingham Australian ballot (newspaper source, disclosed; the town posts no 2026 results document): Amy Howlett won a three-year seat (391-73 over William Crowther) and Bonnie North (315) and Dalila Hall (251) won the two one-year seats -- the vacancy remainders of the departed Peter Golec and Elijah Zimmer -- in an eight-candidate field

offices.title: Lister
offices.org_name: Town of Rockingham Board of Listers

sources.note: 17 V.S.A. section 2646: towns elect a board of listers of three on staggered three-year terms
Town of Rockingham, Lister's Office page (rockinghamvt.org): 'The Listers are elected to assess property in the Town of Rockingham'; the page names Paul Noble and Tad Dedrick
The Commons, report of the March 3, 2026 Rockingham Australian ballot (newspaper source, disclosed; the town posts no 2026 results document): Paul Noble was re-elected Lister, uncontested

Town of Rockingham, 2025 Annual Report (July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025), 'TOWN OF ROCKINGHAM ELECTED OFFICIALS 2024-2025' table and the printed 2026 warning, read in the town's document library: listers Tad Dedrick (2024-2027) and Paul Noble (Chair); Michael Stack resigned from a term ending in 2025 and no successor is published, so the third seat is unfilled

offices.title: Trustee of Public Funds
offices.org_name: Town of Rockingham Trustees of Public Funds

sources.note: 17 V.S.A. section 2646: towns elect three trustees of public funds on staggered terms

Town of Rockingham, 2025 Annual Report (July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025), 'TOWN OF ROCKINGHAM ELECTED OFFICIALS 2024-2025' table and the printed 2026 warning, read in the town's document library: Trustees of Public Funds Pat Fowler (to 2028) and David Lambert (to 2028); no third trustee is named, so one seat is unfilled

offices.title: Library Trustee
offices.org_name: Rockingham Free Public Library Board of Trustees

sources.note: Rockingham Free Public Library, bylaws: the board has nine trustees, three elected yearly to three-year terms

Rockingham Free Public Library, Board of Trustees page (rockinghamlibrary.org): the current trustees are Margo Ghia, Virginia Driscoll, Virginia Massucco, Mike Sola, Bonnie North, Martha Rowley, and Carol Blackwood; two seats are vacant (the board's May 21, 2026 agenda carries a Board Vacancy item)

The Commons, report of the March 3, 2026 Rockingham Australian ballot (newspaper source, disclosed; the town posts no 2026 results document): Carol Blackwood and Ginny Massucco were elected library trustees at the 2026 meeting. Blackwood had first joined as a 2025 appointee per the town report table, and Sola joined as a 2023 vacancy appointee but sits under an elected term in that table, so both are recorded as elected

Town of Rockingham, 2025 Annual Report (July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025), 'TOWN OF ROCKINGHAM ELECTED OFFICIALS 2024-2025' table and the printed 2026 warning, read in the town's document library: the elected officials table prints a 'Trustee of the Campbell Fund' heading with no holder's name, so the post is created without a membership

offices.title: Justice of the Peace
offices.org_name: Town of Rockingham Justices of the Peace

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): lists fourteen Rockingham justices of the peace and one 'Vacant' seat: Stuart Brown, Carol Buchdahl, Mark Condon, Patricia Fowler, Dennis Harty, Amy Howlett, Charlie Hunter, Chris Kibbe, Sally MacPhee, Paul Obuchowski, Richard O'Donnell, Peter Stickney, Gloria Vancor, and Deborah Wright (the town report's BCA list agrees; it prints 'Chris Kibbee' where the certified listing has Kibbe). The post carries fourteen filled seats of the fifteen the voters fill. Paul Obuchowski and Dennis Harty also hold Village of Bellows Falls offices; their memberships reuse those person records
